title: JRE 2299 - Dave Smith
guestBio: Dave Smith is a stand-up comedian, libertarian political commentator, and podcaster. He's the host of the "Part of the Problem" podcast, as well as a co-host of the "Legion of Skanks” podcast.
tldr: Dave Smith discusses his libertarian political philosophy and critiques of government overreach
Conversation explores comedy, stand-up craft, and the current state of the comedy industry
Dave shares perspectives on media narratives and how information is controlled and distributed
Discussion touches on the podcast landscape and how independent media has changed political discourse
Dave talks about his 'Part of the Problem' podcast and the Legion of Skanks collaboration
Topics include personal freedom, individual liberty, and skepticism toward institutional authority
recap:
Joe sits down with Dave Smith, comedian and libertarian political commentator, for a wide-ranging conversation that covers everything from stand-up comedy to political philosophy and media criticism. Dave brings his characteristic irreverent take on authority and institutions, diving into why he believes government solutions often create more problems than they solve. The conversation naturally flows between personal anecdotes from Dave's comedy career and broader philosophical discussions about freedom and individual liberty.

Dave talks about his experience in comedy and how the craft has evolved, touching on the pressures comedians face and the importance of maintaining creative freedom. He discusses his podcasts, particularly how 'Part of the Problem' has allowed him to explore political commentary without the constraints of traditional media. Joe and Dave bond over their skepticism toward mainstream narratives and the ways alternative media platforms have democratized information sharing.

Throughout the episode, Dave makes sharp observations about how power structures maintain control through media messaging and cultural narratives. He's articulate about the libertarian perspective without being preachy, using humor and real examples to illustrate his points. The conversation feels like two smart people who don't take themselves too seriously, riffing on current events, the absurdities of government, and what genuine freedom might actually look like in practice.

keyMoments.label: Dave explains his libertarian philosophy and why he's skeptical of government solutions
Discussion about comedy, stand-up craft, and maintaining creative freedom as a performer
Dave talks about launching and running 'Part of the Problem' podcast independently
Conversation on media narratives, information control, and how alternative platforms challenge mainstream messaging
Dave shares insights about the Legion of Skanks podcast and collaborative comedy projects

quotes: The government doesn't solve problems, it just creates new ones while claiming to fix the old ones.
Podcasting and independent media have given us the ability to reach people directly without the filter of corporate media gatekeepers.
Comedy is freedom. If you're not allowed to say what you think, you're not free.
The most dangerous thing to power is an informed population that can think for themselves.
Stand-up comedy is the last honest form of communication because it's just you and the audience with nowhere to hide.
